SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
File No. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 2388 C
S.S.C, Special Branch. Station
Date. April 8, 1941
REPORT
Subject. Mrs. M. SCHOLTZ or SHOLTOVA - Enquiry from the British Consulate-
General.
Made by. D.S.I. Wittinsky, Forwarded by. C.D.I. Tsorum.

Reference the attached communication
received from the British Consulate-General on the
subject of Mrs. M. Scholtz, further enquiries were
conducted during the course of which it transpired
that the information, originally received at the
offices of the Java China Japan Line, 153 Szechuen
Road, to the effect that no passengers arrived in
Shanghai aboard the s.s. "Straat van Malacca", when
she berthed here, on the 13-1-41, was erroneous. It
has now been learned that a number of passengers have
arrived from the South, their names etc., however,
being unavailable owing to the fact that the passenger
list has been, inadvertently, mislaid.

With the arrival of the s.s. "Straat van
Malacca" here, on the 31-3-41, endeavours were made,
through the agents of the Java China Japan Line, to
obtain a duplicate of the passenger list from the
purser but efforts made in this direction proved to
be abortive.

Extensive but discreet enquiries made, with
a view to gleaning information from other sources as
to the present whereabouts of Mrs. Scholtz proved,
likewise, to be without success.

（批：Copy to Mr Box）
（印：SPECIAL BRANCH）

FILE
O. Wittinsky
D. S. I.
A.C. (Special Branch).

日期：1941年4月8日
报告
事由：M. SCHOLTZ 或 SHOLTOVA 女士——来自英国总领事馆的查询——
制作人：副督察 Wittinsky，转呈人：首席侦探督察 Tsorum。

参照附件中收到的英国总领事馆关于 M. Scholtz 女士事宜的来函，随后进行了进一步调查，在此期间发现，最初从四川路153号爪哇中国日本轮船公司（Java China Japan Line）办事处获得的信息——即“马六甲海峡”号（s.s. "Straat van Malacca"）轮船于1941年1月13日在此靠岸时，船上并无乘客抵达上海——是错误的。现已获悉，有一批乘客从南方抵达，但由于乘客名单被不慎遗失，其姓名等信息目前无法获取。

随着“马六甲海峡”号轮船于1941年3月31日抵达此处，曾试图通过爪哇中国日本轮船公司的代理人，从船务长处获取乘客名单的副本，但在此方向上的努力均告失败。

为了从其他来源搜集有关 Scholtz 女士目前下落的信息，进行了广泛而谨慎的调查，结果同样未能成功。

（批注：抄送 Box 先生）
（印章：特务科）

归档
O. Wittinsky
副督察
助理专员（特务科）。

PASSPORT & REGISTRATION OFFICE,
BRITISH CONSULATE-GENERAL,
P.O. BOX 259,
SHANGHAI.
26th March, 1941.

Dear Mr. Sharman,

Your letter D9388(c) of the 17th
February regarding Mrs. Milda Scholtz. I have again
heard that this lady is supposed to be in Shanghai
having arrived on the "Straat Van Malacca" after
being deported from Singapore to Shanghai. We have
also heard that she intends to try to proceed to
Canada.

Have you been able to discover whether
the woman has arrived and if so can you let me have
any additional information? Sorry to worry you like
this.

Yours sincerely,

V. Sharman, Esquire,
Assistant Commissioner,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
SHANGHAI.
page_data.zh:
护照及登记办公室，
英国驻上海总领事馆，
邮政信箱 259，
上海。
1941年3月26日。

亲爱的 Sharman 先生：

关于您2月17日发出的编号为 D9388(c) 的信件，涉及 Milda Scholtz 女士一事。我再次听到消息说，这位女士据称已在从新加坡被驱逐至上海后，乘坐“马六甲海峡”号（"Straat Van Malacca"）抵达上海。我们还听说她打算尝试前往加拿大。

您是否已查明该女子是否已抵达？如果已抵达，能否向我提供任何补充信息？很抱歉这样打扰您。

此致
敬礼，

V. Sharman 先生，
助理专员，
上海公共租界工部局警务处，
上海。

制作人....副督察 Wittinsky，........转呈人 Mason 巡官。

关于捷克斯洛伐克籍 M. Scholtz 或 Sholzova 女士的调查，根据手头掌握的信息，她从新加坡被驱逐，并应于1941年1月13日乘坐“马六甲海峡”号轮船抵达此处，调查显示，至今尚无名为上述姓名的人抵达上海。
        目前无法提供其下落的信息，但若获得相关信息，将立即提交进一步报告。

                                        O. Wittinsky.
                                        副督察

page_data.en:
CONFIDENTIAL

Mrs. Milda Scholtz alias Scholzova
nee Milda Legeding.

Mrs. Scholtz claims to be a Czecho-Slovakian, born at
Riga, Latvia, on 24th August, 1894. She speaks German,
Russian, Lettish, English, Malay, Dutch, Danish and Polish.
She first came to this country in 1931 in possession of pass-
port No. 42/1119"31 issued at Shanghai on 12-7-31 and
valid until 21-9-41. She is the proprietor of the "Prestige"
dress shop in Capitol Building, Singapore, and was formerly
the owner of the "Smart" dress shop in Eu Court Building,
having associated with her in the latter business Madame Galardi.

2. She claims her Czecho-Slovakian nationality because of her
marriage to her second husband who was a Czecho-Slovakian and
whom she divorced in 1934.
X
3. She first came to notice in 1938 in Shanghai, for being
closely connected with an Austrian engineer in the employment
of a Netherlands concern. The Austrian was engaged in drug
smuggling.

4. She left Shanghai and went to Manila where it is reported she
came to the notice of the Manila Police and was ordered to leave.

5. She came to Malaya in 1930 and came to the notice of the
Singapore Police as a sly prostitute, drug addict and she was
also suspected of drug smuggling.

6. In 1931 she went to Ipoh where she went into partnership
with a Madame Kovach in the dress shop business called
"Salon des Modes". She came under the notice of the Ipoh Police as
a sly prostitute and while she was there she became the mistress
of a number of men.

7. She has travelled extensively in Japan, China, the Philippines,
Germany, Austria, Czecho-Slovakia, Holland, Denmark, and it is
believed other European countries also. She is known to have
visited Germany and Czecho-Slovakia in 1934 and 1937.

8. In 1938 she came under the adverse notice of the Police for
speaking very strongly in favour of Hitler's policy over the
Sudetan (sic) question. It was also noticed at this time that she
was well supplied with funds and was frequently seen with Germans
in Singapore.

9. At the time of the Munich crisis of 1938, she contacted a
number of Service officers and frequently spent afternoons at
the Seletar Grange Hotel, where she met naval officers from
the naval base. In conversation with a naval officer whom
she met at Raffles Hotel she displayed a remarkable knowledge
of and interest in naval matters, and tried to obtain further
information from this officer. She revealed knowledge of the
very recent arrival in Singapore of a warship which was not
generally known outside Naval circles. She also asked unusually
intelligent questions about the movements and equipment of warships
and also revealed that she had a knowledge of the movements of
the American fleet in Asiatic waters. She disclosed the fact that
she knew quite a number of American Naval Officers. It is
possible, of course, that she met these officers when employed
as a prostitute. She is known to have displayed exceptional
interest in the disposition of Naval, Military and Air Force
units and of steps taken for the defence of the Colony.

X : Possibly a typographical error for "1928"
page_data.zh:
机密

Milda Scholtz 女士，别名 Scholzova
婚前姓 Milda Legeding。

Scholtz 女士声称是捷克斯洛伐克人，1894年8月24日出生于拉脱维亚里加。她会说德语、俄语、拉脱维亚语、英语、马来语、荷兰语、丹麦语和波兰语。她于1931年首次来到本国，持有1931年7月12日在上海签发的第42/1119"31号护照，有效期至1941年9月21日。她是新加坡国会大厦（Capitol Building）“Prestige”时装店的所有者，此前曾是欧法院大楼（Eu Court Building）“Smart”时装店的店主，在后一家店铺中与 Galardi 夫人有合作关系。

2. 她声称拥有捷克斯洛伐克国籍，是因为她与第二任丈夫结婚，该丈夫是捷克斯洛伐克人，她于1934年与其离婚。
X
3. 她于1938年在上海首次引起注意，原因是与一名受雇于荷兰公司的奥地利工程师关系密切。该奥地利人从事毒品走私活动。

4. 她离开上海前往马尼拉，据报道她在马尼拉引起了警方的注意，并被勒令离开。

5. 她于1930年来到马来亚，并因作为暗娼、吸毒者而引起新加坡警方的注意，她还涉嫌参与毒品走私。

6. 1931年她前往怡保（Ipoh），与一位 Kovach 夫人合伙经营名为“Salon des Modes”的时装店。她因作为暗娼而引起怡保警方的注意，在那里期间，她成为多名男子的情妇。

7. 她曾在日本、中国、菲律宾、德国、奥地利、捷克斯洛伐克、荷兰、丹麦以及据信其他欧洲国家广泛旅行。已知她曾于1934年和1937年访问过德国和捷克斯洛伐克。

8. 1938年，她因强烈支持希特勒在苏台德（原文如此）问题上的政策而引起警方的负面关注。当时还注意到她资金充裕，并经常在新加坡与德国人在一起。

9. 在1938年慕尼黑危机期间，她接触了一些军职人员，并经常在实里达格兰奇酒店（Seletar Grange Hotel）度过下午时光，在那里她会晤来自海军基地的海军军官。在与她在莱佛士酒店结识的一名海军军官交谈时，她表现出对海军事务非凡的了解和兴趣，并试图从该军官处获取更多信息。她透露了一艘战舰最近抵达新加坡的消息，而这在海军圈子之外并不为人所知。她还就战舰的动向和装备提出了异常精明的问题，并透露她了解美国舰队在亚洲水域的动向。她披露了她认识相当数量的美国海军军官这一事实。当然，有可能她是在从事妓女职业时结识了这些军官。已知她对海军、陆军和空军部队的部署以及为保卫殖民地所采取的措施表现出异常的兴趣。

X ：可能是“1928”的印刷错误

page_data.en:
-2-

10. In 1939 she applied for British naturalisation, but her
application was refused. She has been heard to say that she
applied for naturalisation in order to escape the possibility
of internment.

11. In June 1939 she went to Saigon but was refused permission
to land by the French police to whom she is also known. She then
went to Kobe, Japan, and later returned to Singapore.

12. At the outbreak of war she turned up at Central Police
Station with other German nationals expecting to be interned.

13. From various sources it is known that she has on occasions
expressed anti-British and pro-German views and to have claimed
that her relatives are fighting for Germany.

14. She is known to have contacted an Austrian doctor in Shanghai
who is under the notice of the Shanghai Police and who visited
Europe in 1938 and returned to Shanghai just before the outbreak
of war. This Austrian, Misrini, instructed another alien female
who is under surveillance in Singapore to make contact with
Scholtz. Misrini alias Miorini, has been identified as an
espionage agent, now (1940) in Shanghai.

15. Her address was in the Address Book of the late Italian
Consul, Singapore, Captain Tarabocchia, who left here for Italy
via Japan at the beginning of October 1940. Presumably she was
known to him.

16. On 7-2-40 Mrs. Scholz was warned against trying to send
money to her sons in Germany through a friend in Holland.

17. She was ordered to leave Malaya under Defence Regulation 22
and left by the s.s. "Straat van Malacca" on 3-1-41 bound for
Shanghai.

18. Before departure she sold up her dress shop and gave out
that she was going to Shanghai, hoping to be able to work her way
over to Canada where she knew a Canadian who wanted to marry her.
It is not known who this Canadian is.

Special Branch.
S.S. Police.
30-12-40.

The American Consul-General,
Singapore.

10. 1939年，她申请加入英国国籍，但申请被拒。有人听到她说，她申请入籍是为了逃避被拘禁的可能性。

11. 1939年6月，她前往西贡，但被法国警察拒绝登陆，她在法国警察那里也有案底。随后她前往日本神户，后来返回新加坡。

12. 战争爆发时，她与其他德国国民一起出现在中央警署，预期会被拘禁。

13. 从各种渠道得知，她曾多次表达反英和亲德观点，并声称她的亲属正在为德国作战。

14. 已知她接触过上海的一名奥地利医生，该医生在上海警方有案底，曾于1938年访问欧洲，并在战争爆发前夕返回上海。这名奥地利人 Misrini 指示另一名在新加坡受监视的外籍女性与 Scholtz 建立联系。Misrini，别名 Miorini，已被确认为间谍特工，目前（1940年）在上海。

15. 她的地址出现在已故意大利驻新加坡领事 Tarabocchia 上尉的地址簿中，该领事于1940年10月初经日本离开此地前往意大利。推测她为领事所认识。

16. 1940年2月7日，Scholz 女士受到警告，不得试图通过一位在荷兰的朋友向她在德国的儿子们汇款。

17. 根据《防卫条例》第22条，她被勒令离开马来亚，并于1941年1月3日乘坐“马六甲海峡”号轮船离开，前往上海。

18. 出发前，她卖掉了她的时装店，并宣称她将前往上海，希望能设法辗转前往加拿大，因为她认识一位想娶她的加拿大人。目前尚不清楚这位加拿大人是谁。

特务科。
海峡殖民地警务处。
1940年12月30日。

CONFIDENTIAL REPORT Date January 20, 1941.
Subject Mrs. M. SCHOLTZ or SHOLZOVA - Inquiry from the British Consulate-General.
Made by D.S.I. Vittinsky. Forwarded by Supt. Mason.

With reference to the attached communication
received from the British Consulate-General re Mrs. Milda
Scholtz or Sholzova, I beg to report, that the s.s. "Straat
van Malacca" arrived here from the South on January 13th, 1941.
Enquiries at the shipping offices of the Java-China-Japan Line,
133 Szechuen Road, revealed that the boat did not carry any
passengers destined to Shanghai.

The information available at present re Mrs. Scholtz
is to the effect, that she is a dress-maker by occupation,
was formerly a prostitute and is reported to have been involved
in drug trafficking. Whilst at Singapore, she sought the
company of naval officers with a view to collecting information
of military nature. She is reported to be of pro-German
feelings. (Sp. Br. file D. 9388 C.)

A further report re Mrs. Scholtz will be submitted
should information re her arrival, subsequent movements and/or
activities be available.

Keep in view &

Dear Mr. Robertson,

holding Czech passport 42/1119/31 issued in Shanghai

information you may already have, or subsequently obtain,
about her.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. P. REGISTRY
B. D. 938810
21 8 39

Mrs. Milda SCHOLZ alias SCHOLZOVA
nee LEGSDIN, Czechoslovakian

Aboard the m/v "Felix Roussel" which sailed
from Saigon on June 30, 1939 en route to Japan was
Mrs. Milda SCHOLZ alias SCHOLZOVA nee LEGSDIN, of
Czechoslovakian nationality. She holds passport
No. 42/1119/31 issued on July 12, 1931 by the
consulate of the Czechoslovakian Republic at Shanghai
and renewed on September 22, 1936 at Singapore.
Not being in possession of a French consular visa
she could not disembark at Saigon as she intended
to do and continued her voyage aboard the same
vessel with the destination for Kobe.

Mrs. SCHOLZ was a dress-maker at Singapore.
It is reported that formerly she was a prostitute
and was involved in drug trafficking and that at
Singapore she sought the company of naval officers
with a view to collecting information of military
nature. She is reported to be of pro-German
feelings.

As Mrs. SCHOLZ expressed her intention to
apply to the Governor-General for permission to
reside in Indo-China, I have the honour to request
you to be good enough to advise me should the
person in question leave Shanghai for Indo-China.

Lil
Cop
Ruy

米尔达·肖尔茨（Milda SCHOLZ），别名肖尔佐娃（SCHOLZOVA）
婚前姓莱格斯丁（LEGSDIN），捷克斯洛伐克籍

1939年6月30日从西贡启航前往日本的法国邮轮“费利克斯·鲁塞尔”号（m/v "Felix Roussel"）上，载有捷克斯洛伐克国籍的米尔达·肖尔茨（Milda SCHOLZ），别名肖尔佐娃（SCHOLZOVA），婚前姓莱格斯丁（LEGSDIN）。她持有1931年7月12日由捷克斯洛伐克共和国驻上海领事馆签发、并于1936年9月22日在新加坡续期的第42/1119/31号护照。由于未持有法国领事签证，她无法按原计划在西贡下船，遂继续乘坐同一艘船只前往神户。

肖尔茨女士在新加坡的职业为裁缝。据报她曾为妓女，卷入毒品贩运，且在新加坡期间刻意结交海军军官，意在收集军事情报。据报她持有亲德情绪。

鉴于肖尔茨女士表示有意向总督申请在印度支那居住的许可，本人荣幸地请求阁下，若当事人离开上海前往印度支那，敬请惠予通知。

Lil
副本
Ruy
